headline: The growth hormone data
body: contradicts itself and nobody tells you

headline: Camp one says
body: GH reliably adds height in short kids. | Meta-analyses of *idiopathic short stature* found treated groups ended **0.84 standard deviations** taller than controls. | And it is dose dependent: 0.16 to 0.28 mg/kg/week gives under 4 cm, while 0.32 to 0.4 mg/kg/week gives **7 to 8 cm**.
punch: One study found 9.5 cm in males over untreated controls.

headline: Camp two says
body: GH does nothing, or makes it worse. | A 1997 study of boys who were short but **not** GH deficient. | Untreated averaged **162.0 cm**. GH treated averaged **154.2 cm**.
punch: Nearly eight centimetres in the wrong direction.

headline: Both are real
body: Neither side is making its evidence up. | The disagreement is inside the literature, not between honest and dishonest people. | You are usually only shown one half.
punch: So how are both true at the same time?

headline: Different populations
body: The optimistic pooled analyses lean on idiopathic short stature cohorts, and many were uncontrolled. | The bad results come from controlled comparisons in non deficient boys followed through puberty. | Different starting point. Different design.
punch: Who got studied changes the answer completely.

headline: Which is the real lesson
body: Not that GH works. Not that it does not. | The effect depends on who you are. | Nobody quoting you a single number has told you which cohort it came from.
punch: Ask which group. Every single time.

headline: Now the cost
body: Where gains do happen they run to roughly **$35,000 per inch** of adult height. | That is years of daily injections. | For less than one shoe size.
punch: Efficacy and value are separate questions.

headline: And for normal height
body: Every trial above studied **short** children. Idiopathic short stature or diagnosed deficiency. | I could not find a trial testing GH for height in normal statured people, and there are obvious reasons nobody would run one. | So numbers quoted for that group are being transferred from a different population.
punch: Data about short children is not data about you.

headline: What GH actually does
body: GH recruits *resting zone chondrocytes* into the proliferative pool. | It decides how many cells enter the production line. | *IGF-1* then expands the cells already dividing.
punch: GH sets how many start. IGF-1 sets how far each goes.

headline: Which is why
body: They are not interchangeable. | Recruiting cells and expanding cells are different operations. | Maximising one does not substitute for the other.

headline: And your bloodwork
body: Serum IGF-1 reports **liver output**. | The growth plate makes its own IGF-1 and responds to that. | GH also hits plate stem cells directly through *JAK/STAT*, bypassing the liver entirely.
punch: A normal IGF-1 does not mean your plate is supplied.

headline: The delivery problem
body: Raise systemic IGF-1 and it rises in every IGF-1 responsive tissue you have. | The dose limit is set by everything else, not by the growth plate. | That is why cartilage targeted delivery exists as a research programme.
punch: You run out of headroom before the plate is optimal.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms. Real citations. No protocols.
